title: openFDA (api.fda.gov)
questions: most reported adverse reactions for a drug
drug recalls by classification and year
medical device adverse event reports trend

key_only: more than 1,000 requests a day (120,000 with a key)

manual.how: Open the links in INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser (openFDA answers JSON without a key), save each page under the shown name and upload. For whole datasets use https://open.fda.gov/data/downloads/ (zipped JSON partitions) and upload the extracted files.

cache.why: Searches are small; openFDA refreshes most datasets weekly and FAERS quarterly. data/ is reused within a run.

redistribution.why: openFDA content and data are public domain under a CC0 1.0 dedication unless otherwise noted (https://open.fda.gov/license/).

notices: openFDA data are not validated for clinical use. Adverse event reports are voluntary, unverified reports: a report does not show that a product caused the event, and report counts are not incidence or risk rates.
citation: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, openFDA: {dataset}, api.fda.gov, retrieved {retrieved_long}.

audit_hooks.why: A report that uses openFDA adverse-event counts must say they are spontaneous reports, not incidence rates or proof of causation.

clarify: Adverse events: count reports or count reactions? One report lists several drugs and reactions; say which is counted.
Which dates: when FDA received the report (receivedate) or when the event happened? Recalls: report_date or recall_initiation_date?
All recall classes, or Class I (most serious) only?
